about: Meno, «Del giuoco del Meno» (pp. 78-79) of the Turin rulebook «Primi elementi e regole del giuoco de' tarocchi» (Torino, Soffietti, 1787; the page seen again on the image for this file): the reverse game, in which the winner is «chi fa meno punti» (p. 78). It is described in one paragraph: it is played with four cards as at Sedici, eight as at Trent'uno, or with 25 cards for two players, 25 for three, 19 for four, 15 for five, 13 for six and 11 for seven; the answers are in the suit asked, a trionfo on a trionfo, and never a revoke; the penalties of the other rules hold for Meno too (pp. 78-79). The section says nothing of how the cards are counted, what is done with the cards that are not dealt, who leads, whether a void player must trump, the Fool, or what is paid. Where the section is silent the file follows Dummett 1980, p. 269, or our decision; each leaf says which. Marks: [D] documented, [R] our reading, [S] sources silent.

torino1846.cite: L. B., Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, part I (Grammatica del giuocatore), Torino, Serra, [1846]

dummett1980.cite: M. Dummett, The Game of Tarot, London, Duckworth, 1980; chapter XIII, pp. 258-279 (partial scan held, p. 268 missing)

prammatica1846.cite: L. B., Prammatica del giuocatore di tarocchi ossia regole indispensabili per gli amatori di simile passatempo, Torino, Serra, [1846] (separate issue, cover dated 1846, deposited 27 December 1845; reprinted from the same setting, same pages, as part II of Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, Torino, Serra, [1846])

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 78: the table of hands runs from «in due persone» to «con undici carte in sette persone».

direction.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35, 37: «gli altri sempre a destra procedendo»: play passes to the right.

first_dealer.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 16: cards are turned up for each side, «se viene prima da questa parte un Trionfo, mischierò io»: the side that first receives a trionfo shuffles and deals first. General rule of the book, not repeated in the section.

cut_by.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 16-17: the player on the dealer's left cuts («di dar a coppare a chi ti siede a sinistra»); if he declines the next on the left, if all decline the dealer deals as the pack lies. General rule of the book, not repeated in the section.

cut_min.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 16: «Una carta sola non si può coppare»: the page forbids only a cut of one card; that each part keeps at least two cards is our reading.

dealer_rotation.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 78-79 do not say who deals next; ours after Torino [1846], part I, p. 18: «a chi vien dopo a destra».

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 78: «sempre vince colui, che di tutti gli altri compagni fa meno punti»: no partners, the player with the fewest points of all the others wins.

deck.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 78: the section does not name the pack; the hands of 25 cards for two and for three players and of 11 for seven presuppose the whole pack of 78 (pp. 9-10).

trump_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 13: «l'Angelo, il quale è il XX., appresso noi prende il Mondo»: the trionfi rank by their printed numbers, with the Angel XX above the World XXI («l'usanza, che in questo caso fa legge»); the Fool stands outside the order. The Meno section gives no order of its own; the general rule applies.

suit_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 11-13: in swords and batons the larger number takes the smaller; in cups and coins «la carta di numero inferiore prende quella di numero superiore, eccetto le figure» (the ace takes the two up to the ten); the courts stand above every numeral. [R] The order among the courts, King, Queen, Knight, Jack, is read from their points 5, 4, 3, 2 (pp. 13-14) and from the list of p. 10.

card_points.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 13-14: «Ogni Re conta cinque punti. Ogni Donna conta quattro punti»: king 5, queen 4, knight 3, jack 2, the Angel 5, Bagatto 5, the Fool 5. How Meno is counted (pp. 78-79 do not say) is written in hand.count.group.

fool.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 78-79 do not mention the Fool; ours: the excuse, as in the other long games of the book.

fool_exchange_to.source: [R] Torino [1846], part I, p. 33 (Venticinque for three): «onde chi ha presa o coperta la mano non abbia ad averne danno»: the plain card for the Fool goes to whoever took the trick; Torino 1787, pp. 77-78 says the same of Permesso for five to seven: «la carta poscia del Folle si dovrà sempre dare a chi ha preso». Carried over (revision 9, answer 10 of the lead session). Other reading (stood until revision 8): the card goes to the opposing side.

options.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 21 (rule 10): «quanto si giuochi la partita semplice, qualunque sia il giuoco, che facciasi»: the stake of the simple game is settled before the deal. The book names no amount (p. 15 plays «un quattrino per ciascuna partita» as an example); the list of choices is the table's.

variants.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 78: «si può giuocare con quattro carte, come al Sedici»: four cards to each player. [R] Read as one deal with the number of cards only; whether the deals are repeated as at Sedici and when the game ends is not said. The tie rule of the base game holds (result.tie).

count.source: [S] Ours: the form is played at the numbers of seats where a hand of four cards has a winner often enough and rarely more than one (a check of 200 hands by random players at each number of seats: no winner at most 15 %, more than one winner at most 50 %). With four cards that holds for two and three seats only; with more seats most hands are shared by several players. The book of 1787 (p. 78) names the form for any number of seats.

hand_size.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 78: «con quattro carte, come al Sedici».

group.source: [R] As Sedici (Torino 1787, p. 78: «come al Sedici»); counted singly, Fool an ordinary trionfo.

plain_value.source: [S] Ours as Sedici, after Dummett 1980, p. 269: plain cards 0.

replace.what: the value of a plain card counted singly

trump_order.source: [R] As Sedici (Torino 1787, p. 78: «come al Sedici»): the Fool an ordinary trionfo, the lowest, taken by Bagatto (pp. 14, 38).

card_points.source: [R] As Sedici (Torino 1787, p. 78: «come al Sedici»); counted singly, Fool an ordinary trionfo.

fool.source: [R] As Sedici (Torino 1787, p. 78: «come al Sedici»); counted singly, Fool an ordinary trionfo.

variants.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 78: «con otto carte, come al Trent'uno»: eight cards to each player. [R] Read as one deal with the number of cards only (Torino [1846], part I, pp. 30-31; Dummett 1980, p. 269); whether the deals are repeated as at Trent'uno is not said. The tie rule of the base game holds (result.tie).

count.source: [S] Ours: the form is played at the numbers of seats where a hand of eight cards has a winner often enough and rarely more than one (a check of 200 hands by random players at each number of seats: no winner at most 15 %, more than one winner at most 50 %). With eight cards that holds for two to five seats; with six and seven seats most hands are shared by several players. The book of 1787 (p. 78) names the form for any number of seats.

hand_size.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 78: «con otto carte, come al Trent'uno».

group.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, pp. 30-31: «le carte si contano ad una ad una».

plain_value.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 31: «I punti si contano precisamente come a Trent'uno al più»: a plain card counts one.

trump_order.source: [R] As Trent'uno (Torino 1787, p. 78: «come al Trent'uno»): the Fool an ordinary trionfo, the lowest, taken by Bagatto.

card_points.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 31: «I punti si contano precisamente come a Trent'uno al più».

fool.source: [D] Prammatica [1846], p. 6: in Trent'uno al meno «il Matto è considerato come semplice tarocco».

left_out.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 32, of Trent'uno al meno: «nella vola non perde uno solo, ma tutti»: the player who takes every trick is the only winner and all the others pay him. [R] Carried to Meno, as the same page reads: usually one player loses.
left_out.why: Not played: the core plays settle.premiums only as an empty list (core/modules/settle.js). The book of 1787 (pp. 78-79) does not name the vola at Meno.

hand_size.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 78: «con venticinque carte in … con venticinque carte … carte in sette persone».

face.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 78: not said; the general rule of the long games is covered cards (p. 59).

dealer_extra.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 78 does not say what is done with undealt cards; ours: none extra, no discard, as Dummett 1980, p. 269.

dead.source: [S] Ours after Dummett 1980, p. 269: the undealt cards lie out of play.

follow_suit.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 78-79: «se io giuocherò Bastoni, tu mi risponderai … risponder Trionfo, e non mai rinegare»: the answer is in the suit asked, a trionfo on a trionfo.

first_leader.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 35 (general): «Chi è a destra di chi dà, comincia».

replace.what: the count and the first lead of Meno

next_leader.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 37 (general rule of the book): «Colui, che or ultimo ha preso la mano … deve essere il primo a giuocare».

must_trump.source: [R] Torino [1846], part I, p. 36 prints the duty for Partita and the games after it: «si risponderà e prenderà con un Trionfo»; carried back to this game. Torino 1787, p. 49 (Baronetti) prints the same duty: «se non ho carte della medesima sequenza prendo con Trionfi».

must_overtrump.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 78-79 are silent; ours: no duty, as Nice 1930, p. 283 and Piedicavallo 2008, p. 13.

group.source: [S] Ours after Dummett 1980, p. 269: counted in pairs (forms of 25, 19, 15, 13, 11 cards).

replace.what: the count and the first lead of Meno

winner.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 78: «guadagna chi fa meno punti»; «sempre vince colui, che di tutti gli altri compagni fa meno punti».

game_points.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 78-79: the book names no game points and no payment; the stake of the simple game is agreed for every game (p. 21).

replace.what: who wins and who pays in Meno, and what happens when the fewest points are equal

tie.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 78-79, Torino [1846], part I, pp. 31-32 and Dummett 1980, p. 269 say nothing of equal fewest points. Ours: the players with equal fewest points all win and the one with the most points pays each of them a stake; when all are equal nobody pays. Other version (revision 9): a tie is a hand played out and nobody pays.

replace.what: who wins and who pays in Meno, and what happens when the fewest points are equal

unit.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 21: the simple game is paid in the stake agreed before the deal, «qualunque sia il giuoco, che facciasi».

amount.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 21: «quanto si giuochi la partita semplice, qualunque sia il giuoco».

mode.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 78-79 name no payment; the fewest points win (p. 78: «sempre vince colui, che di tutti gli altri compagni fa meno punti»). Read after Torino [1846], part I, p. 32, said of Trent'uno al meno: «nella vola non perde uno solo, ma tutti»: outside a vola one player loses, the one with the most points, and he alone pays the winner; players equal on the most points all pay. Other reading (revision 9, ours): each other player pays the winner.

replace.what: who wins and who pays in Meno, and what happens when the fewest points are equal

kind.source: [S] Ours: the book describes a hand («la partita») and prints no payment; the marche are settled after every deal, the match ends after one round of dealers (match.dealer_rounds); the greatest balance wins, equal balances are a draw («pace»).

dealer_rounds.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 78-79 are silent on the length of a match and on payment. Ours: one round of dealers, as many deals as players. Other version, for the forms of four and eight cards: a race to a set number of points, «non meno di cinque», as Prammatica [1846], pp. 11-13 has it for Sedici and Trent'uno (an analogy; it is not said of Meno). The table may agree on two or three rounds.

replace.what: the length of a match in Partita for three, Dottore and Meno

effect.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 79: «Le leggi però, che militan pe' trasgressori … ancora per chi giuoca al Meno»; the penalty of a revoke is the simple game to all (pp. 33-34, 38).
